questions.question: Which keywords are available in a Robot Framework suite without any imports?

options.text: Keywords from the BuiltIn library
Robot Framework language statements
Keywords from SeleniumLibrary
options.explanation: SeleniumLibrary must be explicitly imported

options.text: Keywords from all Standard Libraries
options.explanation: Only BuiltIn is imported automatically; other standard libraries need explicit import

questions.question: What are the two main sources for importing external keywords into a suite?

options.text: Libraries
Resource files
JSON configuration files
options.explanation: JSON files are not used for keyword imports

options.text: Python scripts directly
options.explanation: Python code must be packaged as a library, not imported directly

questions.question: What are the three types of libraries in Robot Framework from a user perspective? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Robot Framework Standard Libraries
3rd Party / External Libraries
Custom Libraries
System Libraries
options.explanation: System Libraries is not a category in Robot Framework

options.text: Built-in Libraries
options.explanation: BuiltIn is one standard library, not a category

questions.question: What are Robot Framework Standard Libraries?

options.text: Libraries shipped with Robot Framework that are available without additional installation
Libraries that must be downloaded from PyPI separately
options.explanation: Standard libraries are included with RF installation

options.text: Libraries created by the user for their project
options.explanation: User-created libraries are Custom Libraries, not Standard

options.text: Only the BuiltIn library
options.explanation: Standard libraries include BuiltIn, Collections, String, OperatingSystem, and more

questions.question: What are 3rd Party / External Libraries?

options.text: Libraries developed by community members that must be installed separately
Libraries that come pre-installed with Robot Framework
options.explanation: 3rd party libraries require separate installation

options.text: Libraries written by the user for their specific project
options.explanation: These are Custom Libraries, not 3rd party

options.text: Libraries that can only be used with a commercial license
options.explanation: 3rd party libraries can be open source or commercial

questions.question: How do you import a library into a suite or resource file?

options.text: Use the Library setting in the *** Settings *** section followed by the library name
Use the Import setting in the *** Settings *** section
options.explanation: The setting is called Library, not Import

options.text: Use the @library decorator in the test case
options.explanation: Robot Framework doesn't use decorators for imports

options.text: Add the library to a configuration.yml file
options.explanation: Libraries are imported in the *** Settings *** section

questions.question: Is the library name case-sensitive when importing?

options.text: Yes, the library name is case-sensitive
No, library names are case-insensitive like keyword names
options.explanation: Library names are case-sensitive, unlike keyword names

options.text: Only on Linux; case-insensitive on Windows
options.explanation: Library names are case-sensitive on all platforms

options.text: Case-sensitive for custom libraries only
options.explanation: All library names are case-sensitive

questions.question:
Analyze these library imports:

```robot
*** Settings ***
Library    OperatingSystem
Library    Browser
Library    DatabaseLibrary
```

Which statements are correct? (Select all that apply)

options.text: OperatingSystem is likely a Robot Framework Standard Library
All three libraries are imported by name (not path)
These libraries must be in the Python module search path
These imports are case-insensitive
options.explanation: Library names are case-sensitive

questions.question: What happens when a library is imported?

options.text: All keywords from that library become available in that suite or resource file
Only selected keywords from the library become available
options.explanation: All keywords become available, not just selected ones

options.text: The library is compiled and optimized for execution
options.explanation: Libraries are not compiled; they're imported at runtime

options.text: A copy of the library is created in the project directory
options.explanation: Libraries are referenced, not copied

questions.question: What is unique about the BuiltIn library compared to all other Robot Framework libraries?

options.text: It is the only library imported invisibly and automatically in every scope
It is the only library written in Python
options.explanation: Many libraries are written in Python; automatic import is BuiltIn's unique feature

options.text: It is the only library that can be used in both test cases and tasks
options.explanation: All libraries can be used in both; automatic import makes BuiltIn unique

options.text: It is the only library shipped with Robot Framework
options.explanation: Multiple standard libraries ship with RF; BuiltIn is unique in being auto-imported

questions.question: How can libraries that are NOT in the Python module search path be imported?

options.text: By using the path to the Python module
They cannot be imported; they must be in the search path
options.explanation: Libraries can be imported by path if not in search path

options.text: By using the --force-import flag
options.explanation: There is no such flag; use path instead

options.text: By copying them to the Robot Framework installation directory
options.explanation: This is not necessary; use path-based import

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of resource files?

options.text: To organize and store keywords and variables used in multiple suites
To store test cases that can be shared across projects
options.explanation: Resource files don't contain test cases

options.text: To configure Robot Framework execution settings
options.explanation: Resource files contain keywords and variables, not configuration

options.text: To generate documentation for the project
options.explanation: Documentation is generated by libdoc, not resource files

questions.question: What is the main difference between suite files and resource files?

options.text: Resource files do not contain test cases or tasks; suite files must contain them
Resource files use different syntax than suite files
options.explanation: They share the same syntax

options.text: Resource files cannot import libraries
options.explanation: Resource files can import libraries

options.text: Suite files cannot contain keywords
options.explanation: Suite files can contain keywords in *** Keywords *** section

questions.question: If a resource file imports a library, where are that library's keywords available?

options.text: In any suite that imports that resource file
Only in the resource file itself
options.explanation: Keywords are available in importing suites too

options.text: Only in suites in the same directory as the resource file
options.explanation: Availability depends on import, not location

options.text: Globally in all suites in the project
options.explanation: Only in suites that import the resource file

questions.question:
Consider this structure:

```robot
# common_keywords.resource
*** Settings ***
Library    SeleniumLibrary
Library    DatabaseLibrary

*** Keywords ***
Login As User
    # keyword implementation

# test_suite.robot
*** Settings ***
Resource    common_keywords.resource

*** Test Cases ***
Test Login
    Login As User
    Open Browser    url    chrome
```

What keywords are available in test_suite.robot? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Login As User (from resource file)
SeleniumLibrary keywords (imported in resource file)
DatabaseLibrary keywords (imported in resource file)
BuiltIn library keywords
Only Login As User, not library keywords
options.explanation: Library imports in resource files are also available to importing suites

questions.question: How do you import a resource file into a suite or resource file?

options.text: Use the Resource setting in *** Settings *** section followed by the path to the resource file
Use the Library setting followed by the resource file name
options.explanation: Library is for libraries; Resource is for resource files

options.text: Use the Include setting followed by the resource file path
options.explanation: The setting is called Resource, not Include

options.text: Resource files are automatically discovered and don't need importing
options.explanation: Resource files must be explicitly imported

questions.question: What file extension should resource files use?

options.text: .resource (recommended for clarity)
.robot (required)
options.explanation: .robot works but .resource is recommended for clarity

options.text: .py (Python extension)
options.explanation: Resource files use RF syntax, not Python

options.text: .txt (plain text)
options.explanation: .resource or .robot extensions are recognized by IDEs

questions.question: Why is the .resource extension recommended over .robot for resource files?

options.text: To make it clear what they are (resource files vs suite files)
.robot extension doesn't work for resource files
options.explanation: .robot works but .resource is clearer

options.text: .resource files load faster
options.explanation: Performance is identical; it's about clarity

options.text: IDE extensions only recognize .resource files
options.explanation: IDEs recognize both .robot and .resource

questions.question:
Analyze these imports:

```robot
*** Settings ***
Resource    local_keywords.resource
Resource    D:/keywords/central_keywords.resource
```

What types of paths are used? (Select all that apply)

options.text: First import uses a relative path
Second import uses an absolute path
Both imports use absolute paths
options.explanation: First is relative, second is absolute

options.text: Both imports use relative paths
options.explanation: Second is absolute with drive letter

questions.question: When a relative path is used to import a resource file, where is it resolved relative to?

options.text: The data file (suite or resource file) that is importing it
The current working directory where robot command was executed
options.explanation: Relative paths are relative to the importing file, not CWD

options.text: The Robot Framework installation directory
options.explanation: Paths are relative to the importing file

options.text: The root suite directory
options.explanation: Paths are relative to the importing file, not root suite

questions.question: If a relative path for a resource file is given and the file is not found relative to the importing file, where else does Robot Framework search?

options.text: In the Python module search path (PYTHONPATH)
In the user's home directory
options.explanation: RF doesn't automatically search home directory

options.text: In the Robot Framework installation directory
options.explanation: RF uses Python module search path, not its own directory

options.text: Nowhere else; the import fails
options.explanation: RF also searches the Python module search path

questions.question: How can the Python module search path be influenced? (Select all that apply)

options.text: By setting the PYTHONPATH environment variable
By using the --pythonpath CLI argument when executing robot
By editing the Robot Framework configuration file
options.explanation: Use PYTHONPATH or --pythonpath, not a config file

options.text: By installing libraries with pip
options.explanation: pip installs to a location already in search path

questions.question: What path separator should be used in Robot Framework import paths?

options.text: Forward slashes / on all operating systems (strongly recommended)
Backslashes \ on Windows, forward slashes / on Linux/Mac
options.explanation: Forward slashes work everywhere and are recommended

options.text: Backslashes \ on all systems
options.explanation: Backslashes require escaping and cause issues

options.text: Either forward or back slashes work equally well
options.explanation: Backslashes require escaping; forward slashes are strongly recommended

questions.question: Why are forward slashes / recommended over backslashes \ for paths, even on Windows?

options.text: Backslashes are escape characters in Robot Framework and can cause issues
Windows doesn't support backslashes in Robot Framework
options.explanation: Windows supports backslashes, but they require escaping

options.text: Forward slashes are faster to process
options.explanation: Performance is not the reason; it's about escaping complexity

options.text: Robot Framework only runs on Linux
options.explanation: RF runs on all platforms; forward slashes work everywhere

questions.question:
Which of these path examples is correct and recommended?

```robot
A) Resource    ..\resources\keywords.resource
B) Resource    ../resources/keywords.resource
C) Resource    ..//resources//keywords.resource
D) Resource    ..\\resources\\keywords.resource
```

options.text: B - uses forward slashes (recommended)
A - uses backslashes (Windows standard)
options.explanation: Backslashes work but require escaping and are not recommended

options.text: C - uses double forward slashes
options.explanation: Double slashes are incorrect

options.text: D - uses escaped backslashes
options.explanation: While this works, forward slashes are simpler and recommended

questions.question: Why should absolute paths be avoided when importing resources?

options.text: Absolute paths are typically not portable across different environments
Absolute paths don't work in Robot Framework
options.explanation: Absolute paths work but are not portable

options.text: Absolute paths are slower to resolve
options.explanation: Performance is not the concern; portability is

options.text: Robot Framework syntax doesn't support absolute paths
options.explanation: Absolute paths are supported but not recommended

questions.question: When are relative paths considered portable?

options.text: When they are related to the importing data file and part of the project structure
Relative paths are never portable
options.explanation: Relative paths within project structure are portable

options.text: Only when they use absolute directory references
options.explanation: That's contradictory - absolute vs relative

options.text: All relative paths are always portable
options.explanation: Only those within project structure are reliably portable

questions.question: What is the most stable and recommended way to import resource files and libraries?

options.text: Use the Python Path/module search path
Use absolute paths to ensure exact location
options.explanation: Absolute paths are not portable; Python path is more stable

options.text: Use relative paths from the root suite
options.explanation: Python path is more stable than relative paths

options.text: Copy all resources to each suite directory
options.explanation: This creates duplication; use Python path instead

questions.question: What is the advantage of using Python module search path for imports?

options.text: Each suite can use the same import path regardless of its location in the project
Imports are faster
options.explanation: The main advantage is uniform import paths, not speed

options.text: No configuration is needed
options.explanation: Python path must be configured when executing robot

options.text: Libraries are automatically installed
options.explanation: Python path doesn't install libraries, just makes them findable

questions.question:
Compare these import approaches:

```robot

Resource    common/keywords.resource
```

What are the advantages of Approach B? (Select all that apply)

options.text: More uniform import paths across different suites
Independent of suite location in project hierarchy
More stable when project structure changes
Works without any configuration

options.text: Automatically creates the resource file if missing
